trip.title: England and Greece 2026
trip.public_summary: An October 10–17 discovery journey through England and Athens, building ministry relationships and planning future Hope Sojourns journeys.
trip.public_description: From London to Northern England and Athens, this October 2026 discovery trip focused on listening to ministry leaders, sharing worship and fellowship, and learning how future teams could support local work. The trip concluded with mentor meetings in London to finalize details for the upcoming England journey and the Athens journey in July.

dailySummaries.title: Saturday, October 17 — Closing the Discovery Trip
dailySummaries.content:
On the final day of this discovery trip, I met with my mentor in London again. We continued our conversations and finalized further details for the upcoming England journey and the Athens journey in July.

Looking back over October 10–17, the trip brought together travel, worship, ministry visits, recorded conversations, and time to plan. In Northern England, I learned more about the Light Group and its work with people experiencing homelessness. In Athens, I listened to ministries serving refugees and people experiencing exploitation.

The trip ends with relationships and next steps to carry forward. These visits have helped inform future planning; the details for each journey will be shared through its own trip information as they are confirmed. Thank you for following along and praying for this work.

dailySummaries.title: Friday, October 16 — Planning the Next Journeys in London
dailySummaries.content:
Back in London, I met with my mentor to work through details for the upcoming England journey and the Athens journey in July. After visiting ministries and listening to their leaders, this was time to bring those conversations into the planning process.

The photographs also record quieter moments around a meal and time in the city. Alongside the travel and ministry visits, these conversations helped connect what I had learned with the practical work of preparing future journeys.

We finalized some of the details together. This is part of the preparation that happens before a team travels: making room for thoughtful conversation and considering how a future visit can support the people already serving in each place.

dailySummaries.title: Thursday, October 15 — Shining the Light of Jesus in Athens
dailySummaries.content:
Today I met with Meredith and Ana from **Νέα Ζωή (New Life)** and learned about their work in Athens’ brothel districts. They have an amazing heart for serving people who are being exploited, entering places many of us would be afraid to go. I also connected with Diana from New Life by text.

As I listened, this thought stayed with me: **“They step into some of the darkest places on earth to shine the Light of Jesus.”**

But that needs an important clarification: Jesus is already there. He is not afraid to go into those places. We often are.

Meredith and Ana’s work challenged me to think about what it means to follow Him—to move toward people who are suffering, even when their circumstances make us uncomfortable. Their heart for this ministry was a reminder that the people they serve deserve to be seen, loved, and treated with dignity.

I also had a brief opportunity to connect with **Hellenic Ministries**. They serve refugees and share the Gospel with them. Although this was a quick touchpoint, it introduced me to another ministry to learn more about as we consider future opportunities in Greece.

Today offered much to reflect on: the courage to go, the willingness to listen, and the reminder that wherever God calls us to serve, He is already at work.

dailySummaries.title: Wednesday, October 14 — From England to Athens
dailySummaries.content:
Today took me from England to Athens for the Greece portion of this discovery trip. After an early flight from Gatwick, the focus shifted to meeting ministries and exploring opportunities for future Hope Sojourns teams.

I met with New Start Ministries, Refugees Refuge, and Porta Ministries & Albanian Church of Athens. I recorded interviews during these visits so I could share more of their stories and help others hear directly from the people doing the work.

The purpose of these meetings is to listen and learn: to understand each ministry’s calling, discover its needs, and consider how a visiting team could come alongside the work already happening.

The photographs from around Victoria Square capture a small part of the city surrounding these conversations. Behind every ministry name are people and relationships. These visits are an opportunity to begin getting to know them.

dailySummaries.title: Tuesday, October 13 — More Time in Northern England
dailySummaries.content:
Today gave me more time to learn about the Light Group and its ministry in Northern England. I recorded a conversation with Paul and a longer interview about the Light Group’s work. These conversations continued the learning that began yesterday in Leeds—understanding the ministry and considering how future Hope Sojourns teams might support it.

The day’s pictures also capture another side of the visit: the Minster’s stained glass, views across Nelson, and the green hills, stone cottages, and dry-stone walls of the surrounding countryside. Among the photographs is the Wuthering Heights pub, set against the landscape of Northern England.

This part of the trip is about building relationships and listening. Before bringing a team to serve alongside a ministry, I want to understand its work, the people it serves, and where our participation could be useful.

dailySummaries.title: Day 2 — Monday, October 12: London to Halifax
dailySummaries.content:
I checked out of my Airbnb in London and walked about five minutes to King’s Cross station. I arrived around 8:30 a.m., which turned out to be fortunate: my 9:10 train to Leeds had been canceled. I went straight to the information desk, where they told me I could take the 8:40 train instead. That put me on my way about half an hour earlier than planned.

When I arrived in Leeds, Dave, Bryan, and Josh met me at the station. We went to Leeds Minster, where we joined a street outreach. We spoke with several people experiencing homelessness and offered them hot tea.

Afterward, we returned to the Minster for the Light Group’s weekly gathering. The Light Group is led by David Fawcett and serves communities throughout Northern England. Its ministry helps people experiencing homelessness work toward getting off drugs, becoming self-sufficient, and finding housing. The group also has a two-year training program for people learning to become pastors to those experiencing homelessness and addiction.

David explained an important distinction in how they describe their work: they don’t call people “marginalized.” Instead, they do ministry *in the margin*. The phrase points to where they go to meet people without turning that place into a label for the people themselves.

The gathering began around 12:30 in the Minster’s café area. For a few hours, people shared coffee and snacks, talked, played games, and enjoyed one another’s company. After that, we had about 30 to 40 minutes of worship, with singing, Gospel sharing, and open conversation. Josh and I sang and led the group in worship.

While we were practicing **“Lean on Me”** in the sanctuary, a woman came in. I didn’t think much of it at first. After we finished, I went over, introduced myself, and asked if she was the caretaker. She said she wasn’t, then told me that her sister had recently died and that the family planned to hold the funeral in that sanctuary. She had come back to see the space again so she could plan the service.

She began to cry and told me she had been hesitant to come in. Before arriving, she had asked God to give her a sign that holding the service there was the right decision. Hearing Josh and me sing gave her that sign. She told me that **“Lean on Me” was her sister’s and her favorite song when they were growing up.**

It was a moving moment—one that made the song feel especially meaningful as Josh and I later led the group in worship. There is a video of the two of us singing **“Lean on Me”** inside the Minster.

After the worship time, we drove from Leeds to Halifax. We stopped at two pubs for refreshments, then went to dinner with a group of 12 people to celebrate the birthday of a Light Group volunteer. It was a wonderful evening of good food, laughter, fellowship, and meeting new people.

Dave lives in Halifax, and I’m staying at his house tonight.

dailySummaries.title: Arriving in London: God With Me Every Step
dailySummaries.content:
My flight left last night at 11 p.m., and I flew overnight directly to London, England. I navigated Heathrow without any delays, found the Underground—the Tube—and rode to King’s Cross station. By then, I was getting very sleepy.

After leaving the train, I set out to find my Airbnb. It wasn’t easy to locate, and the directions were unclear, but I eventually made it inside and found my room. I had thought I was booking the entire flat. Surprise! My room is just big enough for a bed and my two backpacks. The flat has three bedrooms, one toilet room, and one shower room. Even with the unexpected arrangement, it is comfortable.

I headed back to King’s Cross for dinner and enjoyed a delicious meal at The Parcel. Along the way, I found Platform 9¾—a fun Harry Potter reference. I considered going inside, but the line was more than an hour long. Instead, I took a stroll to the canal before returning to my room.

Tonight, I’m hoping for a good night’s sleep. Tomorrow, I’ll take the train to Leeds to meet David, Bryan, and Josh.

Travel can be hard on the body, mind, and spirit, including our emotional outlook. But God is with me every step of the way.

dailySummaries.title: Saturday, October 10 — Setting Out for England and Greece
dailySummaries.content:
Today began the journey to England and Greece. I headed to the airport and boarded the overnight flight to London, carrying the purpose of this discovery trip with me: to listen to local ministry leaders, build relationships, and learn how future Hope Sojourns teams could support their work.

The departure photographs capture the beginning of eight days of travel, conversations, and learning. The work ahead would take me from London to Northern England, then to Athens, before returning to London to consider the next steps.

gallery.title: INVISIBLE — shoes left behind in London
gallery.caption: I found these shoes on a London pavement today, just as they appear here. With no one beside them, the scene looks as though a woman simply disappeared. I do not know the full story behind the shoes. But they brought to mind how people experiencing homelessness can feel: present among us, yet unseen—INVISIBLE. Our calling is to notice the person, listen to their story, and remind them they matter.
